comments.textRawHtml: I understand all the comments for piracy, but I also want to point out, I am happy to spend 80€ but I'm not happy to lock in to a 500€+ console I do not own (I own a powerful PC), and this gate keeping from some console vendors, seems like a good reason, to push on this. children.author: chocochunks
children.textRawHtml:
Nah, dawg. It's definitely not unplayable, GTA IV ran at ~20-30 FPS unlocked just moving on 360/PS3 and that was playable. GTA VI's pretty much always 30 FPS on PS5/XSX except in the most demanding scenarios like blowing up multiple cars in an urban area is pretty fucking playable by comparison. Legit comical to call it unplayable. I've played through much much worse. Series S hews closer to GTA IV at launch but even that's better.

Is 60 FPS and everything the same better? Sure, absolutely. 30 FPS is a compromise to get that level of simulation and graphics. I don't think it would be as engrossing with a quarter the NPCs or stupider ones just to hit 60 FPS.

children.author: denkmoon
children.textRawHtml:
If only there were some hardware platform where the buyer could choose their performance level without compromising on things like NPC count. If only…

Playability is a subjective quality, which would be fairly obvious if anyone in the thread thought about it for a moment. 20fps isn’t playable. If the game were on PC, it would be playable. QED.

children.author: chocochunks
children.textRawHtml:
20 FPS is playable. Go get an N64 and a copy of Ocarina of Time and you'll see. You can play the whole game, it has a 20FPS cap with occasional dips under.

It's not a subjective quality. You can play it, you can complete it then it's not unplayable. It might not be what you personally would prefer, but it's not unplayable.

There will be a PC port, just wait. The 30FPS target makes sense on current gen consoles with what they released.
